newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil industry minister criticises new check tax.
newsitem.headline: Brazil industry minister criticises new check tax.

text.p: Brazilian Industry and Commerce minister Francisco Dornelles said the so-called CPMF check tax which comes into force in January next year could have a negative effect on the country's financial markets.

"I think it could have a very negative effect on the stock market. The tax is arbitrary, retrograde and the most backward in the world tax circuit," Dornelles said at a lunch with businessmen in Rio de Janeiro.
He said the tax, designed to raise about 400 million reais a month to help fund health services, was not compatible with a stable economy and low rates of inflation.

"The tax remains hidden with inflation rates of 50 percent a month, but with an expected inflation rate of seven percent a year in 1997 the tax could weigh heavily on the financial markets," Dornelles said.
Dornelles said Brazil's financial markets had "fantastic" potential, and substantial foreign investments of $8 billion to $9 billion a year over the next four years would be reflected in the markets.
"If Brazil has a tax which does not exist in other countries, especially not in the Mercosur member states, then Brazil is at a disadvantage," Dornelles said.
-- Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 5074151
